record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.original_question: Study real Banach spaces X with second-order polynomial numerical index n^(2)(X) = 0. In particular, determine whether such spaces must also satisfy the ordinary numerical index condition n(X) = 0, and answer the same question in the finite-dimensional setting.

evidence.quote: Problem 42. Study the real Banach spaces X satisfying n(2)(X) = 0. For instance, do they satisfy that n(X) = 0? What is the answer for finite-dimensional spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a real Banach space. For a positive integer k, let P(^kX:X) denote the Banach space of continuous k-homogeneous polynomials from X to X, endowed with the supremum norm on the unit ball B_X. For P in P(^kX:X), define its numerical radius by
  v(P) = sup{ |x*(P(x))| : x in S_X, x* in S_{X*}, x*(x) = 1 }.
The polynomial numerical index of order k of X is
  n^(k)(X) = inf{ v(P) : P in P(^kX:X), ||P|| = 1 }.
For k = 1, this reduces to the (ordinary) numerical index n(X).

Questions:
(a) Characterize the real Banach spaces X for which n^(2)(X) = 0.
(b) Does n^(2)(X) = 0 imply n(X) = 0?
(c) Answer (b) under the additional assumption that X is finite-dimensional.
artifact.category_tag: Polynomial numerical index of Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaced foundational papers on the polynomial numerical index (Choi–García–Maestre–Martín and related works) and subsequent studies on spaces with polynomial numerical index 1 or with absolute norms, but did not produce a definitive resolution of whether n^(2)(X) = 0 implies n(X) = 0 for real Banach spaces, either in general or in finite dimensions. The current status appears to be unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: The polynomial numerical index of a Banach space
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces and studies the polynomial numerical index of order k for Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the polynomial numerical index n^(k)(X) used in the problem.

status_evidence.title: Banach spaces with polynomial numerical index 1
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizations of Banach spaces with polynomial numerical index 1 under RNP/Asplund hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature focuses on the polynomial-numerical-index-1 case, not on n^(2)(X)=0.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial numerical indices of Banach spaces with absolute norm
status_evidence.snippet: Computes polynomial numerical indices for spaces with absolute norms.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist but do not settle the implication n^(2)(X)=0 => n(X)=0.
